_comment: The hardware wired to this machine. Replaces moil_camera.yaml,
moil_axis.yaml and moil_monitor.yaml, which were three files because
there were three ROS nodes; there is one process now, so there is one
file. Every key is optional -- a missing key uses the default in
src/models/device/device_config.h, which is the value the rig was
running with. Delete this file entirely and the app still starts.
The app WRITES this file when the display mapping is applied, so
comments and key order are not preserved once that happens.
system: 'yuanman' (Arduino Mega for X/Y/Z + KOHZU CRUX for
yaw/pitch, two ports) or 'yinda' (five ports, one per axis).
SETTLED on this machine, 2026-08-10, by reading Windows itself
(Win32_SerialPort) rather than either source:
COM3 = 'Arduino Mega 2560'      VID_2341&PID_0042
COM4 = 'CRUX USB Serial Port'   VID_267D&PID_1121
So moil_axis.yaml's comment was the correct one and
axis_module_yuanman.py's COM4/COM5 defaults were not -- those are
what the FastAPI server and then the ROS node instantiated, and they
were wrong here, which is why the app reported 'COM5 is not found'.
These numbers are per-machine: re-check Device Manager on any other
rig instead of copying this file.
enable_write_position: sends WRP to zero the position counter after
a home. OFF by default because it has never in fact been sent: the
ROS client made it a no-op, and before that the Python driver's
range guards were inverted so it always refused. Turning it on is a
change to how the hardware behaves, not a restoration.
backend: 'mf' | 'msmf' | 'dshow' | 'any'. Ignored off Windows.
'mf' does not go through OpenCV at all -- it is the Media Foundation
path in camera_mf.cpp, the same API the Windows Camera app uses, and
it picks the camera's MJPG mode (0.25 MB a frame) over YUY2 (18.5 MB).
'msmf' is OpenCV's own Media Foundation wrapper, which measured 21.3
fps at 3040x3040 against dshow's 1.1 (dshow pins the stream to
uncompressed YUY2). Do not change any of this without re-measuring.
capture_format: 'jpeg' reproduces the images the detectors were
tuned against -- the camera node published JPEG q=80 and everything
downstream saw those. 'png' is lossless and now possible (there is
no transport to pay for), but it changes what the detectors see and
costs about a second per 3040x3040 frame to encode.
_measured_on_this_rig_2026_08_10: msmf CANNOT OPEN this camera at all through OpenCV 4.6.0 -- every id,
Media Foundation opens the same device and pulls 3040x3040 frames in
MJPG, NV12 and YUY2, so the camera is fine and the limit is OpenCV's
dshow opens it and reaches 3040x3040, but measured 1.17 fps here --
matching the 1.1 this file already warned about. Asking dshow for MJPG
does NOT help: the fourcc comes back YUY2 either way, so it really is
pinned to 18.5 MB per uncompressed frame.
So this is 1.17 fps against not working at all, not against 21.3.

_comment: Direction -> display number. Written by Monitor Viewer > Setup
Monitor Direction; there is no need to fill it in by hand. Empty
means unmapped, and patterns are refused with that as the reason.
Accepts '1' or 'DISPLAY1'.
